proposal: The Mandate recommends assessing the mismatch between VHA's aging inpatient facilities and where veterans now live, noting that the Asset and Infrastructure Review authorized in 2018 ended when the Senate did not act on commission nominations. It calls for operational alternatives, including expanding community-based outpatient clinics to keep a VA presence in difficult markets without more investment in older campuses, and piloting facility-sharing partnerships with strained local health systems.

status_summary: No infrastructure review of the kind the Mandate describes (a successor to the Asset and Infrastructure Review), no stated policy of expanding outpatient clinics in place of campus investment, and no pilot of facility sharing with strained local health systems were found as of 2026-10-16. Executive Order 14296 (signed 2025-05-09) contains the nearest directed steps: section 5(c) directs VA, consulting DoD and OMB, to develop a strategy for more efficient care that is to include options for treating veterans at selected military treatment facilities and military beneficiaries at VA facilities, with no stated deadline and no published strategy or pilot found, and section 5(b) directs a Manchester, New Hampshire feasibility study toward a full-service medical center, which led to a plan in the FY2027 request for a new VA-owned medical center with comprehensive outpatient services (per a 2026-04-24 letter from New Hampshire's congressional delegation). These parallel the Mandate's outpatient and facility-sharing ideas in direction but differ in design: the sharing partner is DoD rather than local health systems, and the Manchester plan adds a new VA-owned facility. VA's other facility actions point partly the other way or do not address the footprint: it reported $2.8 billion of non-recurring maintenance spending on existing facilities for fiscal year 2025 (including an added $800 million announced 2025-08-21) and announced $4.8 billion for repairs and modernization in 2026 (per Military Times), the FY2027 request seeks over $5 billion for construction including a replacement medical center in Indianapolis, and the VHA reorganization announced 2025-12-15 reduces management layers (regional networks from 18 to 5, per press coverage) while VA says medical center and clinic operations are unchanged; officials have said they would reduce excess at underutilized locations without naming sites. An op-ed and hearing coverage report that VA is ending contracts for two contract-run clinics, which Secretary Collins attributed to quality problems. Senator Moran introduced S. 3388 on 2025-12-08 and Representatives Schmidt and Elfreth introduced H.R. 6595 on 2025-12-10 on DoD-VA resource sharing; GovInfo bill status for S. 3388 states that its text is contained in the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (Public Law 119-60, 2025-12-18), whose section 731 bears the same title, so DoD-VA action plans for resource sharing at military and VA medical facilities are now a statutory direction; no resulting plan was found, and the partner is DoD rather than local health systems. A VA release of 2026-10-14 describes $2.681 billion in further maintenance and upgrade projects at existing facilities in the fourth quarter of FY2026 and the full obligation of a $4.8 billion FY2026 maintenance budget, without any realignment.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14296, 'Keeping Promises to Veterans and Establishing a National Center for Warrior Independence' (published 2025-05-14 at 90 FR 20369), directs VA to commission a feasibility study at the Manchester VA Medical Center (section 5(b), action plan due within 180 days toward a full-service medical center in New Hampshire) and, in section 5(c), directs a strategy, developed with DoD and OMB and with no stated deadline, to deliver VA care more efficiently, first prioritizing shorter access times, with options for treating veterans at selected military treatment facilities and military beneficiaries at VA facilities with reimbursement. It does not direct an asset review, clinic expansion in place of campus investment, partnerships with local health systems, or disposal of property.

VA announces an additional $800 million for its Non-Recurring Maintenance program, bringing fiscal year 2025 spending on that program to $2.8 billion, to repair and update aging health care facilities nationwide (a VA medical center release listing local projects, including HVAC and chiller replacements and the disposal of the Miles City campus); the release describes upkeep of existing facilities, not a realignment of the footprint.

Senator Moran introduces S. 3388, the Sharing Essential Resources for Veterans Everywhere Act, which would require Defense and Veterans Affairs action plans to strengthen resource sharing at military treatment facilities and VA medical centers under existing authority, and does not mention pilots with local or community health systems (House companion H.R. 6595 was introduced 2025-12-10; per GovInfo bill status the text of S. 3388 was later carried into Public Law 119-60, see 2025-12-18).

VA announces a VHA reorganization: Central Office would set policy goals and handle finance, oversight and compliance, while regional networks and operations centers would set operational, quality and performance standards. VA says it is not a reduction in force, expects no significant change in overall staffing and says staffing and operations at medical centers and clinics will not change; changes would follow over 18 to 24 months. The release does not address facility footprint.

The National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (S. 1071) becomes Public Law 119-60. Its section 731, titled improvement of availability of care for veterans from facilities and providers of the Department of Defense, carries the text of S. 3388 according to GovInfo bill status for S. 3388; as introduced, that text directs Defense and Veterans Affairs to develop and implement action plans at military treatment facilities and VA medical facilities to strengthen resource sharing under existing authority, with a public list of sharing agreements, annual briefings to Congress and a 2028-09-30 sunset. It concerns DoD-VA sharing, not partnerships with local health systems, and the enacted wording of section 731 was not read beyond its heading.
timeline.source: GovInfo (Public Law 119-60 and BILLSTATUS for S. 3388)

timeline.event: VA gives Congress details of the VHA reorganization (named RISE) in January 2026 (month-only date), as reported by Military Times on 2026-01-30: regional networks (VISNs) would fall from 18 to 5, with health service areas and a medical operations center; VA announced $4.8 billion for repairs and modernization this year; and Secretary Collins would reduce excess at underutilized locations, without naming sites. The article does not mention closing facilities or clinics.

New Hampshire's congressional delegation writes to the administration asking for release of the Manchester feasibility study and action plan. The letter says a 2026-04-15 VA briefing reported the study was complete, that the White House and VA chose an option, shown in the FY2027 budget request, of a new VA-owned medical center providing comprehensive outpatient services in Manchester, and that an interagency agreement with the Army Corps of Engineers was to begin implementation in April 2026.

Secretary Collins tells a Senate subcommittee that VHA is ending contracts for two contract-run outpatient clinics, in McMinnville, Tennessee (closing 2026-05-31) and Schenectady, New York (closing August 2026), after a review found they did not meet VA standards of care, per an op-ed by a Disabled American Veterans state hospital chairman (2026-05-06). Hearing coverage of 2026-04-30 and 2026-05-20 also describes a contract clinic closure attributed to poor performance. No VA document on the closures was found.

Secretary Collins's written testimony to the Senate Appropriations MilCon-VA Subcommittee on the FY2027 request cites over $5 billion for construction, including a new medical center in Manchester, a replacement medical center in Indianapolis and land acquisition for a replacement in San Antonio, and says VHA is restructuring to streamline operations without reducing staff. The testimony does not address aging facilities as a problem, an Asset and Infrastructure Review or sharing agreements.

VA announces $2.681 billion approved for infrastructure improvement projects in the fourth quarter of FY2026, drawn from a $4.8 billion non-recurring maintenance budget that VA says was fully obligated, for repairs and upgrades at existing medical facilities; the release also cites 43 new health care facilities opened since 2025-01-20 and mentions no consolidation, closure or realignment.

title: Realign VHA's aging facilities: infrastructure review, more clinics, facility sharing
uncertainties: Stage decision (proposed kept; not_started and diverged considered). Basis: the rubric counts a step directed by an order with nothing yet operative as proposed. Executive Order 14296 section 5(c) is such a directed step for one of the Mandate's three components, facility sharing, but with DoD as the partner and efficiency and access as the purpose, so match is parallel and progress sits near the bottom of the band at 8, which also reflects the enacted DoD-VA resource-sharing direction. The Manchester plan is not counted as progress: it adds a new VA-owned facility, although it is outpatient-focused. No strategy under section 5(c), no sharing pilot, no infrastructure review and no clinic-for-campus policy was found, and the facility funding found (non-recurring maintenance of $2.8 billion for FY2025 and $4.8 billion for FY2026, replacement medical center requests) runs against the Mandate's preference for not investing further in older campuses, so diverged is arguable; not_started is arguable because VA and DoD already share resources under existing authority (as S. 3388 itself describes) and the order's strategy is a general efficiency exercise. Searches and queries run: Federal Register queries for the Asset and Infrastructure Review (none since 2025-01-20), build-to-suit leases and Manchester presidential documents; web searches on VA infrastructure review or realignment (earlier pass: only 2021 to 2023 material), FY2027 budget and facilities, Manchester, DoD-VA sharing and the reorganization; this pass added searches on VA-DoD sharing strategy after EO 14296 (no strategy or pilot reported), the Manchester plan after April 2026 (no new release found) and VA footprint realignment (found maintenance funding announcements only); the VA press room page (latest ten releases to 2026-10-07 did not concern facilities). Figures for Manchester and Indianapolis differ between Collins's 2026-04-30 Senate Appropriations testimony and his written testimony for the 2026-05-20 Senate Veterans' Affairs hearing (veterans.senate.gov, read), so amounts are omitted. A newsletter summary of the 2026-05-20 hearing says Collins described a shift toward outpatient and ambulatory facilities, but his written testimony for that hearing does not mention it, so this was not relied on. The $4.8 billion figure for FY2026 comes from Military Times; the VA release for it was not found, and the $2.8 billion figure for FY2025 comes from a VA medical center page that describes the additional $800 million. The reorganization's VISN reduction (18 to 5) and the 24,000 position cut come from Military Times. The 2026-01-28 Senate and 2026-02-11 House statements were read only in the earlier pass. VA's FY2027 budget justification volumes and 2026 GAO work on VHA oversight were not read. The delegation letter is the only source for the Manchester option chosen; the study and plan documents have not been released. The two clinic closures rest on an op-ed and hearing coverage, not a VA document. Freshness pass 2026-10-16: the VA press-room page (ten newest releases, 2026-09-14 to 2026-10-15) showed no release on facility realignment, closures, DoD sharing or Manchester; a 2026-10-07 VA pilot at six medical centers concerned VA.gov account setup with a private vendor, not facility sharing. Web searches on a section 5(c) VA-DoD strategy and on the Manchester plan found no strategy, pilot or published feasibility study after 2026-05-06. GovInfo bill status for S. 3388 lists its latest action as referral to Senate Veterans' Affairs on 2025-12-08 and states that its text is contained in S. 1071, which became Public Law 119-60 on 2025-12-18; the GovInfo public law page lists section 731 under the same title as S. 3388, but the fetched copy was truncated before the section text, so the enacted wording, and any change from the introduced text, was not read. H.R. 6595 showed referral to the House Veterans' Affairs Health Subcommittee on 2025-12-18 as latest action. Two appropriations steps were reviewed and kept out of the timeline as general VA funding rather than realignment actions: the House passed the FY2027 Military Construction and Veterans Affairs bill (H.R. 8469) 400 to 15 on 2026-05-15, with VA major construction below the FY2026 level per CRS, and it was placed on the Senate calendar on 2026-07-14; and a continuing resolution (H.R. 6500, Public Law 119-103, 2026-09-02) funds operations through 2026-12-11 (both per GovInfo bill status). The House-passed bill text was not read beyond CRS figures. A September 2026 executive order on VA-DoD benefits data sharing appeared in search results but was not read and is outside the facility-footprint scope. The enacted text of section 731 of Public Law 119-60 still could not be read, because the GovInfo HTML and PDF copies end near 100,000 to 128,000 characters and the XML path returned a not-found page; a Senate committee report copy of the Senate bill was also cut off before any matching section. A member press release of 2025-12-09 describes the conferenced provision as requiring Defense Health Agency and VA action plans to increase use of military hospitals and enhance resource sharing, which is consistent with the introduced text of S. 3388; it does not give a section number and it predates enactment. EO 14296 was confirmed in the Federal Register API record (90 FR 20369, signed 2025-05-09, published 2025-05-14), and the VA release of 2026-10-14 was re-read and mentions no realignment, closure or sharing.
